title: What Plasmonic Computing Is
definition: Plasmonic Computing: computing with plasmons below the diffraction limit.
description:
Strip Plasmonic Computing to its essence and you get computing with plasmons below the diffraction limit. Simple to say, civilizational to build.

The path runs through Future Computing Paradigms: first nano antennas understanding, then plasmonic logistics prototypes, then loss management operations at scale. Each stage has its own physics, its own economics, and its own failure modes — this database maps all three.

Use the ladder: start with foundations, work through the components and forecasts, run every demo, then attempt the compounded drills. By the final record you will hold a working mental model of plasmonic hulls, grounded in real research and honest about what remains unknown.

title: Real Research Today: Plasmonic Computing
definition: Today's documented research behind Plasmonic Computing.
description:
The road to Plasmonic Computing is already being paved. Intel's Loihi and IBM's TrueNorth/ NorthPole chips advance neuromorphic computing. IBM's quantum roadmap targets 100,000-qubit systems with error correction this decade.

Google's Sycamore and Willow chips demonstrated quantum error-correction milestones. Together these programs form the nano antennas foundation that Plasmonic Computing will build on — the plasmonic logistics results, the loss management methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as plasmonic logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: Readiness Estimator: Plasmonic Computing
definition: Estimates Plasmonic Computing readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Plasmonic Computing components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a plasmonic hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Plasmonic Computing Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Plasmonic Computing: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Plasmonic Computing — computing with plasmons below the diffraction limit.

Phase 1 — Prove (nano antennas): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (plasmonic logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (loss management): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (optical IO): plasmonic hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and labs-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
